$comment: Figma layer path (as in spec.json) -> element inside the entry's target (.ds-email-draft).

Title.$why: The row spans the column in code; Figma's hugs the title and the badge.

Header/Badge.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font. Figma's 6 px sides are the Badge's 2 px padding plus its label's 4 px in code.

To.$why: Figma draws the 1 px line above the row as its own layer; in code it is the row's top border (45 px), so the card's height is the same.

Recipient.$why: Figma's select hugs the name and the address; code's shows the name (the Select trigger shows labels) and hugs it. Figma pads the select's inner Body frame; code pads the trigger itself (Select's own check covers them).

Attachment.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

Rewriting.$why: The row spans the body in code; Figma's hugs the spinner and the words.

Editing.$why: Editing, the field has focus: code draws the ring colour and the focus ring, as Approval Gates' editable arguments do; Figma draws the rest stroke (colors/input).

Message.$why: The text mixes weights (the link is Medium), so Figma reports none.

Tone.$why: The row spans the body in code; Figma's hugs the toggles. While editing, Figma's body is 8 px in (for the field) and the row 8 more; in code the body stays 16 px in and the field reaches 8 px out.

Toggle Group.$why: It hugs its toggles, whose widths follow the font. Figma's 8 px gap is on the group's inner items frame.

Footer.$why: Figma draws the 1 px line above the footer as its own layer; in code it is the footer's top border (45 px).

Footer/Badge.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font. Figma's 6 px sides are the Badge's 2 px padding plus its label's 4 px in code.

Footer/Button.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

Footer/Button#1.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

Line/Text.$why: It takes the room left beside the button, whose width follows the font.

Line/Button.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.
